seo_title: Coca-Cola Case Study: Foodie Creator Whitespace | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read Foodie creators and the cola category for Coca-Cola in four markets and found home cooking at 62.9% of Indian creator content, with cola at 0%.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Soft drinks · 4 markets
h1: Coca-Cola owns the table in 4 markets, Foodie creators own the kitchen
lede: SOMIN read Coca-Cola, 2–5 soft-drink competitors and 5–7 Foodie creators in each of India, the United Kingdom, Mexico and South Africa, from June 2025 to May 2026. Foodie creators were loudest on home cooking and regional discovery, up to 82.9% of their content, where the cola category had 0%. Each market got one SOMIN persona and three pillars.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · Jun 2025 – May 2026 · India, United Kingdom, Mexico, South Africa · Foodies

stats.label: Indian Foodie-creator voice on home cooking

challenge.title: Coca-Cola's voice sits in celebration and sport, like its rivals
challenge.body: Coca-Cola's voice sits in celebration and sport, territory it shares with every competitor. Comparing it with Pepsi, Limca, Corona or Irn-Bru only shows the floor: where the category is crowded and where parity is required. The real question was where the Foodie audience is talking, and whether the cola category is in that conversation at all.

approach.title: Three cohorts and eight content strands in each of 4 markets
points: Ran SOMIN Perspective Studies in every market on three cohorts: Coca-Cola, its competitors and a panel of leading Foodie creators, across four quarters of 2025–26.
Measured share of voice across eight recurring content strands, from home-cooking enablement to sports and event fandom.
Applied a whitespace test: where Foodie creators are loud and the cola category is absent, the territory is open.
Gave each market one anchor SOMIN persona and three pillars, each carrying a SOMIN tension, a strategic angle and an insight story.
Read every trend as share and volume together, so a falling percentage is never mistaken for decline.

findings_title: Home cooking and regional discovery are open in all 4 markets

findings.title: Home cooking is 62.9% of Indian Foodie content, cola 0%
findings.body: Home-cooking enablement made up 62.9% of Foodie-creator content in India, while Coca-Cola and its competitors each had 0.0% there. Coca-Cola put 57.1% of its own voice into shared celebration.

findings.title: Regional discovery: 76.8% in Mexico, 82.9% in South Africa
findings.body: Authentic and regional culinary discovery took 76.8% of Foodie-creator content in Mexico and 82.9% in South Africa. Neither Coca-Cola nor its competitors published in that strand.

findings.title: UK creators split 48.2% home cooking, 43.7% discovery
findings.body: UK Foodie creators put 48.2% into home-cooking enablement and 43.7% into regional discovery, with the cola category at 0.0% on both. Coca-Cola put 69.2% of its voice into shared celebration.

delivered.title: A persona and three pillars for each of Coca-Cola's 4 markets
points: One anchor SOMIN persona per market: India, the United Kingdom, Mexico and South Africa.
Three pillars per market, such as Home-Cooking Confidence, World on Your Table, Reclaim the Roots and Honour the Craft, each tied to a SOMIN tension, angle and insight story.
A whitespace table and quarterly topicality read for every market, with a verdict per strand from whitespace to contested.
A mapped field of strategic angles for each tension, so the creative team can pick one per pillar.
A cross-market plan: lead with a culinary whitespace pillar, hold an everyday-pairing bridge and defend or extend the third pillar.

quote.text: Coca-Cola owns the table. The Foodie creators own the kitchen.

outcome.title: Coca-Cola should lead each market on its culinary whitespace
outcome.body: SOMIN recommends leading each market's creator collaborations on its whitespace pillar: home cooking or authentic discovery. SOMIN moments become the publishing calendar, the everyday-pairing bridge is held with real propositions, and the celebration pillar is defended in Mexico and South Africa with Coca-Cola's existing voice. Same strategic move in every market; the persona and the cultural route in change.

faq.q: Why look at Foodie creators and not only at competitors?
faq.a: Competitors show the floor: where the category is crowded and parity is required. Foodie creators surface food trends before brands do, so where their audience leans in and no cola brand has followed is the differentiation opportunity.

faq.q: What does whitespace mean in this briefing?
faq.a: Whitespace means the creator cohort is active, used as a proxy for audience demand, and the cola category is not. A brand simply being quiet does not count, because its silence may be deliberate.

faq.q: Is the plan the same in every market?
faq.a: The strategic move is the same: lead with a culinary whitespace pillar and keep an everyday-pairing bridge where Coca-Cola already has a foothold. The anchor persona, the pillars and the cultural route in change by market.

faq.q: Why read volume as well as share?
faq.a: In India, the share of creator content on authentic and regional discovery fell from 81% to 37% across the year, but total creator volume grew from 48 to 559 posts. The falling share is a composition effect, not a decline.
